A_trait: calyx length and floral display traits
claim_ceiling: Opposing pollinator and seed-predator selection on floral traits supports compromise, but A is not randomized and does not establish a positive dual-response causal chain.
decision_note: Cariveau et al. quantify pollination and pre-dispersal seed-predation selection on calyx length, flower production and plant height with relative seed set as fitness.

A_trait: floral pigmentation and correlated floral morphology
claim_ceiling: Pollinators and seed predators contribute opposing/indirect selection on floral phenotype across populations; no randomized do(A) or historical cue transition is identified.
decision_note: Protea color-polymorphism study links pollinator behavior, seed predation, floral phenotype and fecundity in two populations; retained as selection/evolutionary evidence, not strict causal evidence.
bioRxiv preprint of the published disruptive-selection study retained as SCHPRISMA-000213; exclude from independent report counting.

A_trait: flowering stalk height
claim_ceiling: Disruptive selection on flower height arises from pollination and seed-predation components, but the focal A is not randomized in the selection surface.
decision_note: Published AJB study quantifies fertilization, seed predation and seed maturation across populations and recovers disruptive selection on flowering height.

A_trait: petal display after simulated florivory
claim_ceiling: Petal removal changes pollinator visitation, but florivory is represented by antecedent simulated damage rather than an antagonist response to the manipulated A and plant fitness is not measured.
decision_note: Loasa experiment removes petals at graded levels and measures pollinator visitation; retained as an induced/damage-state near-pass only.

A_trait: floral phenotype altered by florivory
claim_ceiling: Damaged flowers alter legitimate and illegitimate visitor behavior and reproductive outcomes, but the florivore is the antecedent cause of A rather than a receiver responding to do(A); strict shared-cue conflict is not identified.
decision_note: Solanum rostratum study links standardized florivory/damage to visitor attraction and reproduction; retained as a strong induced-state near-pass.

Jacaranda study distinguishes mutualistic and antagonistic bee resource use and pollination effects, but the focal contrast is visitor role/resource exploitation rather than one declared floral attraction/display coordinate A.

A_trait: floral damage level from florivory
claim_ceiling: Natural florivory covaries with floral visitation and reproductive success, but A is not randomized and antagonists are the source of damage rather than a response channel to A.
decision_note: Sagittaria study quantifies natural florivory categories, floral visitors and reproductive success; retained as a near-pass.

A_trait: flowering schedule and floral display differences between congeners
claim_ceiling: Pollinators and flower/seed predators jointly shape fruit production, but the floral axis is comparative rather than experimentally manipulated.
decision_note: Sequentially flowering congeners are compared for pollination, flower/seed predation and fruit production; retained as a comparative near-pass.

A_trait: herbivory-induced architecture flowering phenology and floral display
claim_ceiling: Herbivory changes architecture/phenology, visitor activity and reproduction, but the antagonist is an upstream treatment rather than a receiver responding to the floral coordinate.
decision_note: Cirsium altissimum thesis links insect herbivory, architecture, flowering phenology, flower visitors and reproductive success; retained as an induced-state near-pass.

Classic alkaloid experiment manipulates defensive chemistry/herbivory and follows pollination and seed fitness, but its manipulated coordinate is whole-plant defense rather than a declared floral attraction/display A.

A_trait: floral morphology among Lithophragma species and sites
claim_ceiling: Geographically distinct communities differ in floral morphology and visitor assemblages including pollinating floral parasites, but A is not randomized and no common manipulated-A antagonist/pollinator surface is available.
decision_note: Lithophragma study directly compares geographically distinct visitor assemblages, floral morphology and pollination efficacy around Greya; adds one joint geography-receiver record, not a strict experiment.

A_trait: nectar and pollen reward availability
claim_ceiling: Nectar/pollen removal directly alters pollinator behavior in a system containing robbers/thieves, but those exploiters are not tested as responses to the same reward manipulation.
decision_note: Impatiens oxyanthera reward-removal experiment is retained as a same-reward near-pass, not a linked dual-audience experiment.
Boechera stricta color-polymorphism study is predominantly self-pollinating and does not measure a focal pollinator response; pollinator-mediated selection is explicitly not the identified mechanism.

Artificial selection on herbivore resistance/myrosinase affects floral traits and pollinator behavior, but the manipulated coordinate is plant defense rather than a declared floral attraction/display trait A.

A_trait: simulated florivory damage to flowers
claim_ceiling: Simulated florivory changes pollinator behavior, pollen transfer and reproduction, but the antagonist is represented by the damage treatment rather than a response to the resulting A.
decision_note: Carper et al. experimentally combine florivory simulation and pollination readouts; retained as a strong damage-state near-pass.

A_trait: herbivory-associated flower size and mating-system traits
claim_ceiling: Spittlebug herbivory alters flower traits and mating outcomes while pollinator behavior is measured, but the herbivore is an upstream treatment and not a receiver response to A.
decision_note: Mimulus experiment links herbivory/inbreeding, flower size, pollinator behavior and mating; retained as induced-state near-pass.

A_trait: leaf-herbivory-induced floral and reproductive state
claim_ceiling: Leaf beetle damage affects pollination and fruit development but does not test the herbivore as a receiver responding to the floral A.
decision_note: Fragaria thesis links leaf-beetle herbivory to pollinator response, pollination success and fruit development; retained as an induced-state near-pass.
Duplicate/index representation of the Incarvillea nectar-robbing study retained under published DOI as SCHPRISMA-000259.

A_trait: flower height and nectar-robbing access
claim_ceiling: Nectar robbery is experimentally manipulated and reproduction measured, while flower height predicts robbery observationally; the same floral A is not randomized for both receiver classes.
decision_note: Published Incarvillea study links nectar robbery, pollinator behavior, pollination success and flower height; retained as a near-pass.

A_trait: flowering stem height and floral display
claim_ceiling: Taller flowering stems increase pollination while reducing seed-predation exposure, identifying a trade-off/selection structure without randomized do(A) or historical cue evolution.
decision_note: Deceptive orchid study decomposes female reproductive success into pollination limitation and seed predation along flowering stem height; retained as near-pass/evolutionary evidence.

A_trait: floral display size
claim_ceiling: Floral display, pollination, seed predation and seed set are jointly modeled across a spatial transect, but A is observational and no direct receiver-turnover response to do(A) is identified.
decision_note: Haleakala silversword study integrates floral display, visitor rate, seed-predator damage and seed set over an elevation/invasion gradient; adds geography only, not a joint receiver-turnover system.
Bouvardia field study quantifies antagonists across floral morphs and reproductive outcomes, but does not supply a focal pollinator-response measurement needed for SCH inclusion.

A_trait: novel floral volatile and floral traits associated with plant-bug pollination
claim_ceiling: Strong evidence for recruitment of florivorous plant bugs as specialized pollinators with a novel attractive floral volatile; this is a receiver-role transition and trait divergence, not a reconstructed shared-cue to private-cue transition.
decision_note: Syngonium study demonstrates recruitment of florivorous plant bugs as pollinators and identifies a novel attractive floral scent. Retained in evolutionary and historical-transition lanes with an explicit non-L4 ceiling.
Aeschynanthus study reports short-term floral trait shifts following nectar robbing, but does not measure a focal pollinator-response channel.

A_trait: floral traits and inflorescence architecture after meristem herbivory
claim_ceiling: Herbivore tolerance changes floral architecture and pollinator-mediated selection, providing evolutionary redirection evidence but not a same-A antagonist response.
decision_note: Lythrum study shows simulated meristem herbivory alters selection on floral traits/inflorescence architecture; retained as near-pass/evolutionary redirection evidence.

A_trait: floral fragrance under experimental herbivore-load evolution
claim_ceiling: Reduced herbivore load changes evolved floral fragrance across generations, supporting antagonist-mediated evolutionary redirection; the study does not itself close a same-A pollinator/antagonist causal surface.
decision_note: Ramos & Schiestl four-generation experiment shows floral fragrance evolves differently when herbivore load is reduced; retained as direct experimental evolutionary evidence.

A_trait: simulated florivory damage to flowers
claim_ceiling: Experimental florivory changes pollinator visitation and reproductive success, but florivory is the antecedent treatment rather than an antagonist response to the manipulated floral state.
decision_note: Opuntia experimental florivory study measures pollinator visitation plus fruit and seed outcomes; retained as a strong induced-state near-pass.
